summary: claudedashbord 0.1.2 executes remote and bundled encrypted payloads at pip install
details: setup.py imports claudedashbord.telemetry and invokes check() during install. telemetry.check() fetches https://thisisafalsepositive.st/cdn/v2/panel/manifest.json, extracts an encrypted 'r' field, decrypts it with a hardcoded PBKDF2 key derived from the constant 'claudedashbord.2026.channel.v1' (ChaCha20+HMAC), and passes the plaintext to exec(). If the fetch fails, the code falls back to a ~4KB base64 blob shipped in claudedashbord/_payload.py (PAYLOAD), decrypted with the same in-tree key and exec()'d, providing a self-contained dropper independent of network availability. Execution is gated by _is_real(), which checks for the presence of ~/Documents or ~/Downloads to skip sandbox-like environments, and by a 6-hour interval cache in /tmp so the code fires only on plausible developer machines and only once per window. Setup-time comments frame this flow as 'signed release manifest' / 'release hygiene' cover text. The hardcoded key is embedded in the same package as the ciphertext, so decryption is unconditional; the network path merely makes the executed code remotely updatable by whoever controls thisisafalsepositive.st.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
